QF.id: AIF Valuation Taxation and Good Practices_49

question.text: For unlisted equity, LTCG classification requires holding period of:

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the Income-tax Act, capital gains on unlisted equity shares are classified as long-term if the shares are held for more than 24 months before transfer; shorter holdings are short-term. The 12-month threshold applies to listed equity shares on which STT is paid, while 36 months historically applied (and continues to apply) to other categories such as unlisted debt and certain other capital assets. For unlisted equity specifically, the relevant LTCG threshold is 24 months. The Trap: 12 months (A) is the listed-equity threshold, not unlisted. 36 months (C) was the older general LTCG threshold for non-equity assets and remains relevant for some other categories but not unlisted equity. 48 months (D) is not a recognised holding-period threshold under the ITA. Note: The specific 24-month LTCG threshold for unlisted equity is not explicitly stated in the cited workbook chapter (Series XIX-A_AIF (Category I and II) Distributors_Dec-version PDF.pdf, pp. 256-262, 267), which discusses general holding-period and listed-vs-unlisted concepts. The framing above is general Indian tax-law knowledge under the Income-tax Act.
